# Lightning

> Lightning (lightningeg.com) is a free personal finance app for salaried people in Egypt. It runs on Android phones and Windows PCs, and counts your accounts, savings, shares, gold and foreign currency in EGP (bank accounts, mobile wallets, cash, gold, bank certificates, EGX shares and funds, US stocks and ETFs, and dollar or other foreign-currency accounts), tracks spending and a monthly budget, and shows how much is safe to spend until payday plus the next three months. It never asks for a bank login: you import CSV statements and review every row. Your money data stays in an encrypted profile on your own phone and computer.

Lightning is a different product from anything else called "Lightning": it is the Egyptian personal finance app at lightningeg.com.

## Key facts

- Who it is for: salaried people in Egypt who want one clear picture of their money in EGP.
- Platform: Windows and Android. The current release is v1.4.2: a Windows ZIP to unzip and open and a signed Lightning Test Android APK (Google Play comes later). The phone holds the ledger, a paired Windows PC borrows it and hands it back over your own Wi-Fi, encrypted, with no server in between, and the phone can read bank SMS into review.
- Price: free to download and use, and nothing is ever locked. After seven days, Lightning asks now and then for a one-time payment; you pay when it is worth it to you and own it forever.
- Currencies and markets: each account keeps its own currency (dollars, euros, riyals and others), counted in EGP at the day's rate or a rate you type, with the gain or loss from the exchange rate shown apart. About 400 US stocks and 70 ETFs on Nasdaq, NYSE and NYSE Arca are priced automatically in dollars. Gulf and European shares can be held with prices you type.
- Bank connection: none. Download a CSV from any bank or wallet, match its columns once, and review each row before it is saved.
- Privacy: money data never goes online. It stays in an encrypted profile on your phone and computer, which talk to each other only over your own Wi-Fi. The only online lookups are the latest prices of what you hold (by ticker symbol) and exchange rates. No account is needed.
- Figures on the site come from Mohab, a fictional 31-year-old salaried user in Cairo, and match the app screens shown beside them.
- Status: a working release you can use with your real numbers today. The release log lists what is still open.

## What it does

- [Home](https://lightningeg.com/): all your money on your phone and PC: net worth across nine places in two currencies (dollar accounts and a dollar brokerage among them), dollars counted in pounds with the gain from the rate, one ledger kept in sync between phone and PC, phone screens, every number with its working, safe to spend, the next three months, what Lightning does for you (bank SMS, rules, weekend-aware bills, search) and a calculator for what a small monthly saving is worth.
- [Features](https://lightningeg.com/features.html): 102 features in twelve groups: the overview page, accounts and transactions, money held for others, bank statement CSV import, budget by category, safe to spend, bills and forecast, shares and funds (EGX, US, Gulf and European), dollars and other currencies, gold and bank certificates, privacy, backups and recovery, typing shortcuts, and your phone and PC.
- [How it works](https://lightningeg.com/how-it-works.html): a monthly routine of about 30 minutes: upload your statements (10 minutes), settle a few rows (5 minutes), then sit down with your numbers (15 minutes).
- [Downloads](https://lightningeg.com/current-status.html): the current Windows ZIP and Android APK, a safe sample year of fictional CSV statements to learn on, and how to give feedback.
- [Sample profiles](https://lightningeg.com/sample-profiles.html): four fictional Egyptian 2026 profiles—Amr (irregular side income), Abdelrahman (steady salary and equity investing), Menna (freelance income), and Fatma (predictable household costs and an emergency reserve)—loadable in Lightning.
- [Release log](https://lightningeg.com/release-log.html): what changed build by build.
- [Contribute](https://lightningeg.com/contribute.html): how anyone can help build Lightning, all on GitHub in the browser with nothing to install: pick a good first issue, comment /take (a bot assigns it; /drop gives it back), change it in a Codespace and open a pull request with "Closes #" and the task number. Questions go on the issue, security problems are reported privately, and non-coders can send app feedback.
- [For Geeks](https://lightningeg.com/forgeeks.html): for developers: where help is needed (Arabic, screens, Python backend, Android and iOS, testing on real PCs and bank formats) and the three steps to a first pull request, then who builds Lightning and why the source is public (source-available, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0), the stack (Python, FastAPI, SQLite with SQLCipher, no frontend build), the test and contract counts, and what is not finished.
- [Roadmap](https://lightningeg.com/forgeeks-roadmap.html): the milestones in order: M1 finish the backend and features and set up the open-source contribution workflow (its items carry the plan codes, like 7B; a task titled [3C] is item C of milestone 3); M2 publish on Google Play; M3 publish on the App Store (iOS, not started). Each lists what is done, in progress and next.
- [Contribute](https://lightningeg.com/forgeeks-guide.html): the one contribution page, in plain words: pick a good first issue and comment /take, change it in a Codespace (GitHub makes your fork), send a pull request; six GitHub terms, what happens after, what to do when stuck, ground rules and the licence, who does what and the merge gates for people and AI teammates, then what Lightning is, how it is built and its terms.

## Guides

Four topics, each the whole picture on one page, with the guides under it:

- [Budget Your Salary](https://lightningeg.com/budget-your-salary.html): Pay the bills first, plan each category, keep a cushion, and spend what is safe.
- [See Where It Goes](https://lightningeg.com/see-where-your-money-goes.html): Bring in a statement once a month and the month reads itself.
- [Know What You Own](https://lightningeg.com/know-what-you-own.html): Add up every place your money sits, take off what you owe, and that is your net worth.
- [Your Data and Devices](https://lightningeg.com/your-data-and-devices.html): Everything stays encrypted on your PC and phone, which meet over your own Wi-Fi.

The guides:

- [Net worth, budget and expense tracker for Egypt](https://lightningeg.com/net-worth-budget-expense-tracker.html): one free app for net worth across bank accounts, wallets, cash, gold, certificates, EGX and US shares and dollars, a monthly budget by category and expense tracking, all in EGP from one ledger, with no bank login.
- [How to calculate your net worth in Egypt](https://lightningeg.com/net-worth-tracker.html): count bank accounts, cash, gold, certificates and shares in EGP, and leave out money held for others.
- [Budget app for Egypt](https://lightningeg.com/budget-app-egypt.html): plan a monthly budget in EGP around your salary.
- [Expense tracker for Egypt](https://lightningeg.com/expense-tracker-egypt.html): see where your money goes each month, by category (the old article on tracking expenses is merged into it).
- [Investment tracker for Egypt](https://lightningeg.com/investment-tracker-egypt.html): gold, bank certificates, EGX and US shares and funds in one EGP portfolio, with what the dollar rate earned you.
- [Dollar savings and US shares tracker](https://lightningeg.com/dollar-savings-tracker-egypt.html): dollar cash and US shares kept in their own currency and counted in EGP at the day's rate, with a holding's gain split into the price part and the exchange-rate part.
- [Cash flow planner](https://lightningeg.com/cash-flow-planner.html): how much is safe to spend before payday, and a three-month forecast.
- [Budget from your bank statement CSV](https://lightningeg.com/bank-statement-budgeting.html): no bank login, just your statement.
- [Offline personal finance app](https://lightningeg.com/offline-personal-finance-app.html): where your data lives and why it stays on your phone and PC.
- [Sync your phone and PC without the cloud](https://lightningeg.com/sync-phone-and-pc-without-cloud.html): one ledger on your phone and PC over your own Wi-Fi, with no account and no server.
- [Track money you hold for others](https://lightningeg.com/track-money-you-hold-for-others.html): keep money you hold for family in your account but out of your net worth.

## Guides (English)

- [Guides](https://lightningeg.com/guides.html): the map: start here, then four topics (budget your salary, see where it goes, know what you own, your data and devices), each linked to its page and to the guides under it. The four articles below sit under it.
- [Why your salary runs out before the month ends](https://lightningeg.com/blog-salary-runs-out.html): hidden, recurring and irregular spending, and how to review a full month.
- [How to split a 20,000 EGP salary in Egypt](https://lightningeg.com/blog-budget-20000-egp.html): a clearly labeled example budget, not a claim about current prices.
- [Emergency fund in EGP](https://lightningeg.com/blog-emergency-fund.html): calculate a reserve from essential household spending.
- [How to budget when your income is irregular](https://lightningeg.com/blog-irregular-income-budget.html): plan around money received and seasonal changes.
